title: Shell command construction does not preserve configured arguments
reasoning: Only the prompt is shell-quoted before the argument list is joined with spaces. A binary path containing spaces or an extra_args element containing whitespace is split into multiple arguments; shell metacharacters in configured values can also become executable shell syntax. This violates the list-of-arguments configuration contract.
reproduction: Configure extra_args as ["--config", "example='hello world'"]. Joining and shell parsing strips the literal TOML quotes, so the CLI receives a different configuration expression from the supplied argument.
recommendation: Build raw argument values and shell-quote every element once at the execution boundary using shlex.join, or pass an argv list directly if the runtime supports it.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests were included that verify argument preservation through shell parsing.
suggestedRegressionTest: Verify round-trip argument preservation for spaces, embedded quotes, dollar signs, and shell metacharacters across prompts, binary paths, and extra_args.
minimumFixScope: CodexAgent command construction and execution-boundary tests.
